chunks: And that which was narrated is: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who circumambulates the House (Kaaba) and then menstruates before she runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: 'When she becomes pure, let her run between al-Safa and al-Marwah.'

There is no prohibition in it against running while she is menstruating, and it merely entails the command for her to run after purification. And we do not say that it is not permissible for her to delay the running until the state of purity; rather, that is the most preferable. And permission was granted to advance it during menstruation out of fear that she might not be able to do it afterwards.

And we have clarified that if the woman menstruates after exceeding half of the circumambulation, she builds upon it (her circumambulation is valid), and whenever she menstruates before half, she repeats from the beginning.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Safa and Marwah (the two hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who menstruates during Tawaf or Sa'i in Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of menstrual interruption during Hajj rituals, specifically addressing the validity of Tawaf and the timing of Sa'i. The Imam clarifies that menstruation does not invalidate the circumambulation already performed, and while delaying Sa'i until purity is preferable, it is permissible to perform it during menstruation if there is a fear of inability to do so later. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility (rukhsah) in ritual purity, ensuring that women are not unduly burdened by the physical constraints of their natural cycle.
